_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
12/31 2:47PM - Happy New Year's Eve! Flakes have been flying and the stoke goes higher than the summit as we ring in the New Year here at Stratton! 

Tonight is shaping up to be the perfect way to welcome the New Year! The Torchlight Parade begins at 8:30pm followed by our annual firework show! For the best viewing experience and to make sure you don't miss any of the action, secure your spot in the Main Base Area by 8:30pm. If you’re looking for a one of a kind view of the show, join us for the Firework Hike to mid-mountain. The Family Buffet dinner in the Base Lodge as well as the 21+ Wild West party at Grizzly’s are now sold out. If you missed out on tickets, there's plenty more options for après including Bar 802, Mulligans, and Green Door! Can’t wait to see you there!

To kick off 2026, you'll find 59 ways down, all of which are set to receive fresh corduroy overnight. For your way up, we are planning on 12 lifts set to spin at 8:30am with the possibility of delays due to wind speeds picking up. Early access will be available for First Tracks pass holders. Snow showers are forecasted to continue through the evening and into New Year’s Day with 2-4 inches in the forecast so keep up those snow dances! Temperatures are expected to dip for tomorrow ranging from 1-5 degrees at the summit and 10-14 at the base. With cold temperatures and strong winds in the forecast, beginner skiing and riding is not recommended from the summit. Colder temperatures sticking around have allowed snowmaking and resurfacing operations to begin and will continue over the next several days as our team works to prepare the mountain for the New Year!

The park scene is coming to life with a 13-foot ramp Retro Halfpipe open and firing on East Byrnes Side, alongside 5 additional features to keep the laps rolling. Tyrolinne Park is also open with 6 features ready to ride.

Happy New Year and I'll see you in the morning for the first update of 2026! 

Safety Tip: Wear an extra layer and keep your face covered.

Holiday week is in full swing with extended dining hours, live music, and special events keeping the Village looking lively. Check out our Holiday Week Dining, Après & Live Music Guide to see what's open, happening, and where the music is at. There’s something for everyone this Holiday week and we couldn’t be more excited to celebrate with you! Click here to check out the upcoming Events Calendar.

The Coca-Cola Tube Park is open! Reservations are recommended to save your spot while availability lasts. Tubing is available in 50 minute sessions starting at the top of each hour. Book now to secure your tickets! Please read the details and policies prior to purchasing your tickets. Hope to see you there!

Ice Skating is open! Lace up and head to the Mill House skating pond for a day or night of winter fun. Enjoy music and a campfire all while gliding under the stars. Book now to guarantee your place on the ice.

Guided Snowmobile Tours are up and running! Explore Stratton after hours with friends and family on a tour to the summit. Be sure to book your spot now to guarantee your spot.

Stay and relish the Green Mountains! Stratton Real Estate is here to help with all your real estate needs. Make your sweet escape a reality.

Reliable cars are the name of the game; that is why we trust Oliver Subaru and Ford. Made for all seasons and all families, check out Oliver Ford and Oliver Subaru for year-round reliability.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Happy New Year’s Eve—Eagle Express is expected to open today! Stay tuned to the website and the Ikon Pass app for real-time terrain updates. Temperatures in the upper 30s and lower 40s are forecast for today. Skies will be cloudy as we move into an active pattern for Thursday and into the weekend. All Sunrise terrain is ungroomed, and early-season hazards exist. Due to early-season conditions, there is no beginner terrain accessible from Moonbeam Express. Apex Express and Sunrise terrain should be considered experts only. Our teams are working hard to bring you more terrain, but please do not duck rope lines into closed terrain. Unseen hazards exist, and you will lose your pass for at least 30 days (at all Ikon Pass resorts). Ring in the New Year with us at the New Year’s Eve Torchlight Parade & Fireworks Show! We have lots of fun events to keep you busy before and after the show. Enjoy a delicious lasagna dinner and a free magic show in Last Chance Lodge from 5:00 — 9:00 p.m. After the New Year’s Eve Torchlight Parade & Fireworks Show, head over to The Thirsty Squirrel to grab a nightcap and sing your heart out to some stellar karaoke.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Good Morning Skiers and Riders! This is Eli with your 5 am snow report for Wednesday, December 31st . Remember the easiest way to get up to date information is on the Ikon Pass app or website.  

Our Mid mountain base is 18 inches, the temperature is 32 degrees, with calm winds and clear skies. 

The Summit base is 32 inches, the temperature is 24 degrees, the winds 16 miles per hour from the west/southwest. 

The base temperature is 9 degrees.  

We will be skiing and riding on 19 lifts, 61 runs, and 578 acres on packed powder and machine made snow.  

This New Year’s Eve, ride the gondola to Thunderhead Lodge for Steamboat’s Dress to Impress Masquerade Party with live DJs, dancing, and a Champagne toast at midnight high above the valley. Tickets are required—get yours at steamboat.com/events and ring in the New Year The Steamboat Way. 

Stay in the know with the Ikon Pass App. Find it in the app store on your mobile device and get lift and trail statuses, conditions updates, and more.  

Ski and Ride with Care and we will see you on the mountain!

Wednesday, December 31, 2025 8:00 AM -- June Mountain will have limited lift and terrain operations today, Wednesday December 31, 2025. Please have grace for our reduced operation, as many of our team members will be honoring Cole Murphy, our fallen patroller, with his family and friends.

We will be operating chairs J1, J2, J3, J4, J6, and the public carpet.

12/31/25  2:54pm Update:  Happy New Year's Eve from Crystal Mountain! We have experienced  another warm, beautiful day in the high country. Conditions were spring-like, especially as the day went on. We have night skiing until 8pm and the fireworks start at 9pm. 

Join us tonight for good turns, good company, and good vibes all around. We will see you next year! 

New year turns on golden snow, Easy lines in morning glow. Friends and laughter, sun so bright, Warm-day turns from first to last light. 

Our annual New Years Bash is today! Close out 2025 with a burst of excitement; no late-night required! Head to Rafters starting at 6:00 p.m. for family-friendly karaoke, live music, and fun contests. At 9:00 p.m., step outside with your mountain community to enjoy vibrant fireworks lighting up the slopes.

Jumpstart your new year with these new deals! Starting January 1st, we're rolling back the pricing on the Anytime and Mid-week 3-day Passes. Ski for as low as $73 a day! No code needed- but hurry, this deal ends on January 11th. Then, on January 6th, we kick off a full month celebration of our founding year, 1962, with $62 now every Tuesday and Thursday through the end of the month. Midweek deals just got a lot sweeter!

Notes for today:
  1. For everyone's safety, sledding is not permitted in our operating area. 
  2. Ski & ride with care. We know you’re excited, and we are too. Please ride responsibly and stay in control today, especially in high traffic area. Take a momement to to read more on our Mountain Safety page!
  3. Obey all mountain closures. Our team is working hard to open terrain as quickly and safely as possible. Closed areas are closed for a reason, so please keep yourself and our team safe by only skiing in open areas. Entering closed areas will result in pass suspension. Thank you!
  4. Book your shuttle today! The Crystal Express Shuttle is free with a reservation, and runs daily through January 4, and continues on weekends and holidays. 
  5. Parking Reservation cancellations are always required if you're not planning on making it up. This includes for advanced bookings and additions from the waitlist. No-show policy applies. Do your part to ensure everyone has access to the mountain. Thank you!
  6. At this time, paid reservations can only be cancelled by emailing SP+ at  CrystalMtnParking@spplus.com with Reservation #, First Name, and Last Name. The Crystal Mountain Contact center cannot process these cancellations.

Mountain Weather 12/31/2025 4:20pm 
 
Synopsis: Warm temps and rain, a bit of a sad way to welcome in 2026. Starting Thursday morning a cut-off low has fallen off track and is wandering down to Mexico stirring up all sorts of warm air and tropical moisture. Thankfully the brunt of the storm is out of the Southwest so there is a decent chance Mt. Rainier will put up its shields and block us from some of the onslaught. Temperatures are slowly dropping as this storm advances but not enough to bring the snow level down to our ridges. No need to hold back on New Year's Eve this year, Thursday and Friday may be better spent inside.

Outlook: There will be a few more days of the dreaded rain before temps drop low enough to put us back below the snow line. Be patient folks, if the models hold there is a very nice treat waiting for us come Sunday! Fingers crossed! Rain rain go away…

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
December 31st, 4:10 PM
Happy New Years Eve Sugarbush sliders! The snowflakes are starting their new year's dance early, with another 1-3 inches expected to flurry in by tomorrow morning! The forecast calls for partly sunny skies and more comfortable temps of low 20's at the base and low teens at the summit.  Winds will be out of the West to toss the fresh snow around creating drifts, scours, and side-stashes. Get ready for some firm and fast groomers today, along with variable conditions as fresh snow will top frozen surfaces.  Tonight, look forward to ringing in the new year in Sugarbush style-we've got the torchlight parade and fireworks, a snowshoe tour, a special NYE party for the kiddos at schoolhouse, and free music by the Grift just to name a few! 

We have over 230 skiable acres served by 10 lifts and 53 open trails, with 36 of those getting a fresh corduroy overnight.  Most natural terrain is closed today in efforts of snow preservation, but we have seen rope drops on the likes of FIS, Black Diamond, Bravo, Exterminator and Encore at Mt. Ellen.  Today’s a perfect day to explore one (or more!) of our five dining options open at Lincoln Peak today. One of my personal favorites is popping up to the Wunderbar for some good vibes and a Schnitzel!  From warm hearty soups to crisp cold beers, we’ve got something for everyone.

Operations are in holiday hours, which means GMX, Super Bravo and Heaven's Gate will get the party started at 8:00 AM. Followed by all other scheduled lifts at 9:00 AM. And in an exciting kickoff to the New Year, the Village Quad is scheduled to open tomorrow at 9:00 AM. The Sugarbush Parks crew has assembled a bumping freestyle setup at Mt. Ellen with 15 features and 2 jumps. Plus, Slowpoke and Sugarbear Forest at Lincoln Peak are home to 13 total features, and newly installed side hits! Snowmaking has shifted to Ripcord and Cruiser, with active guns and whalebacks.  Join us Dec 24th - Jan 1st, for our Holiday Week at Sugarbush, filled with skiing, riding, and festive events for the whole family.  Check out all of our winter events!

All uphill travel routes at both Lincoln Peak and Mt. Ellen are open, check out our uphill travel policy for more info. *Lincoln Peak evening route will stop at the top of Gate House*

Bonjour Tremblant!

There’s no better place to be this New Year’s Eve than on the mountain! Today’s cold, crisp weather is delivering excellent skiing and snowboarding conditions. Whether you’re chasing fresh turns or soaking in the alpine atmosphere, it’s the perfect way to close out the year. Come celebrate with us and make your final runs of the year ones to remember! 

 Some areas of the mountain will open progressively throughout the day as conditions allow, so be sure to check the Snow Conditions page regularly for the latest updates.

3 Snowparks are open, and 15 designated areas are open for Snowshoeing and Alpine Touring.

 Wishing you a wonderful New Year’s Eve, and we hope to see you on the mountain! 

Mountain safety tip of the week: Be careful when using the ski lifts.
Knowing how to board ski lifts is essential to ensure the safety of all users.
 
Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
